Header: Redwood All Hands - May 8 2026
Start time: 2026-05-08 17:00 PDT | Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen, Samir Patel, Leah Gomez, Priya Nair, Marcus Bell, Elena Ruiz, and company-wide channel.

[00:00] Avery Chen: hi everyone, welcome to the may all hands, thanks for joining, um, quick agenda, state of company, product roadmap highlights, infra and reliability, hiring and go-to-market, then q and a.
[00:18] Avery Chen: first off big shout out to the infra team, uh Marcus and crew, we saw a nice improvement in p95 latency month over month, so thank you. there's a lot more to do, obviously, but nice work.
[00:36] Samir Patel: yeah i'll add to that, we shipped the kernel selector improvements last sprint which reduced tail latency for longer sequences, a couple of things are still rough around batching at high conc, but throughput per card is up about 22 percent in our hidden benchmarks.
[01:05] Leah Gomez: on product, Q2 focus is three fold: 1) rollout the per-route cost breakdowns in the console, 2) finish streaming function calling ergonomics, and 3) start the private deployment marketplace play. we're calling the first milestone "billing visibility". we'll be doing a staggered canary.
[01:35] Marcus Bell: quick reliability note, we had that region incident last month; postmortem is in the ops channel. root cause was a combination of a scheduling regression and a KV cache stampede, um i think the transcript might say k v cash sometimes, it's spelled out in the doc. mitigation is: better autoscale guards, stronger backpressure on prefix caching, and a fast rollback path.
[02:04] Elena Ruiz: research update, the evals team ran the open-model comparison across our workloads, the llama-family variant we tested with 4-bit quant did well on cost but had a few hallucination regressions on long form answers; we flagged prompts for deeper evals.
[02:30] Priya Nair: sales, pipeline is healthy; enterprise motion is picking up, a few deals are moving to procurement stage. we're seeing more customers ask for private and dedicated options, and security docs - SOC2, iso, and SSO are the top asks. we'll be pushing a partner enablement playbook next week.
[02:58] Avery Chen: quick finance note - burn is on plan for Q2, revenue showed strong expansion with two new dedi commitments this month, big thanks to Priya and the AE team for closing.
[03:18] Samir Patel: tech highlight - we now have automatic KV cache warmup for frequent prefixes which cuts cold start token cost. still some work on model variant routing when a pinned version is unavailable, fallback logic needs more testing.
[03:42] Audience question (Slack): are we still prioritizing private on-prem customers?
[03:47] Leah Gomez: yes, private is a strategic bet, we have a skeleton for the on-prem install path, and we're working with infra to harden the KMS integrations and audit logs. timeline for a GA-ish beta is late Q3 depending on partner trials.
[04:10] Marcus Bell: to add, the private deployment package will include an ops checklist and HSM/KMS guidance, and we will require an initial security review for big customers.
[04:28] Avery Chen: hiring, we're greenlighted for 18 hires this quarter across infra, product, and sales. we will share the hiring plan and priority roles in the jobs channel.
[04:42] Quick pause for recognition: shout out to the infra on-call who handled the recent incident.
[04:52] Q&A segment begins - employees submit questions via Slido and slack.
[05:00] Q: can we get more detail on the outage?
[05:06] Marcus Bell: sure, briefer version - on 2026-04-21 we saw a region scheduling mismatch that caused a cascade of pod restarts, combined with aggressive cache eviction, leading to elevated latencies. we paged engineering, rolled back the scheduler change, and mitigations are in place. full postmortem link: https://company.docs/postmortems/2026-04-region-outage (see ops channel).
[05:39] Q: will the new billing breakdown affect customers currently on usage plans?
[05:44] Leah Gomez: no disruption, it's visibility-first. customers will see per-route token and cost breakdowns but billing will not change until we announce changes; this is to help customers optimize prompts and routes.
[05:59] Q: roadmap ask - can we prioritize latency improvements for chat workloads?
[06:05] Samir Patel: yes, chat is top priority for latency, we're exploring more aggressive batching heuristics and kernel fusing for short sequences. expect an update next month.
[06:19] Random cross talk and small interruptions, some short filler words, a couple of people dialing in late.
[06:35] Avery Chen: OK let's wrap with next steps - Leah will share the deck and a consolidated FAQ, Marcus will post the runbook updates, Priya will share partner outreach notes.
[06:48] Final remark: thanks team, keep up the momentum, reach out to leadership channels if you have blockers.
[06:56] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription picked up most speakers but sometimes mis-attributed lines, and technical acronyms occasionally garbled (e.g. KV cache -> K V cash). This transcript is intentionally left close to the raw export style.
